channel.title: Neonatal Nutrition Research
channel.description: Clinical research on nutrition, growth, and body composition of premature babies, led by a multidisciplinary team at the UAB Women & Infants Center in Birmingham, Alabama.

item.title: Protein, the Gut Microbiome, and Growth in Preterm Infants
item.description: Our new study published in The Journal of Nutrition explores how protein supplementation may interact with the developing gut microbiome and body composition of extremely preterm infants.

item.title: Feeding the Smallest Patients: What’s Changed—and What Hasn’t?
item.description: Despite major advances in neonatal intensive care, one critical question remains unsettled: are we feeding preterm infants based on the best available evidence—or on outdated habits?

item.title: Early Enteral Nutrition is Linked to Sepsis Prevention
item.description: Infants born extremely preterm (between 23 and 28 weeks of gestation) face a complex journey in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), especially during the first two weeks of life when critical illness is often most severe.

item.title: Does More Early Human Milk Change the Preterm Gut Microbiome?
item.description: For very preterm infants, early nutrition is more than calories—it may help shape lifelong health. Human milk is known to protect against infections, improve growth, and shorten hospital stays.

item.title: How Placental Inflammation Shapes Infant Body Fat Accumulation?
item.description: Histologic chorioamnionitis (HCA), an inflammation of the membranes surrounding the fetus, is a well-known risk factor for preterm birth and adverse neonatal outcomes.

item.title: Finding Balance: Rethinking Growth Goals for Preterm Infants
item.description: For decades, doctors caring for very preterm babies have wrestled with a tough question: What does “good growth” really look like outside the womb?

item.title: Extra Protein for Preemies Boosts NICU Growth, but Does it Last?
item.description: When it comes to extremely preterm (EPT) infants born between 25 and 28 weeks of gestation, nutrition is more than a growth issue; it’s a survival strategy.

item.title: New RCT Analysis Links Early Fortification to Less Severe BPD
item.description: In the world of neonatal intensive care, every milliliter of milk and every calorie counts—especially for extremely preterm (EPT) infants born before 28 weeks of gestation.

item.title: Can Early Vitamin D Supplementation Help Preemies Breathe Easier?
item.description: For babies born extremely early—before 28 weeks of pregnancy—every drop of nutrition counts. Their underdeveloped lungs, fragile bones, and increased risk for complications make early life a high-stakes balancing act in neonatal…

item.title: Can Fortifying Breast Milk Early Help Preterm Babies Grow Better?
item.description: When babies are born too early, giving them the right nutrition is critical — but experts still debate the best time to add extra nutrients (called "fortification") to breast milk.

item.title: The Role of Early Enteral Protein Intake in Lean Mass Accretion
item.description: The first two weeks after birth are a critical period for preterm infants, marked by rapid changes and nutritional challenges.

item.title: The importance of monitoring length and head growth
item.description: A new study proposes a game-changing approach to improving cognitive outcomes in extremely preterm infants.

item.title: Unraveling the Mystery: Do RBC Transfusions Trigger NEC in ELBWI?
item.description: In the intricate world of neonatal care, one of the most dreaded complications is necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC).

item.title: Our Journey Investigating Early & Exclusive Enteral Nutrition
item.description: In our exploration of feeding protocols for preterm infants, we've noticed a stark difference between high-income countries (HICs) and their low- and middle-income counterparts (LMICs).

item.title: 2023 PAS Presentations
item.description: The neonatal nutrition research group at UAB is excited to announce its upcoming research presentations at the 2023 Pediatric Academic Societies Meeting, which will take place from April 28 to May 1, 2023.

item.title: Enriching experiences at the 2023 SSPR meeting
item.description: Our neonatal nutrition research team broadened their knowledge, expanded their network, and engaged with others in their field at the Southern Society for Pediatric Research Meeting this year.
